title: Model metadata
description: What both harnesses need to know about a model, in one shape: a LLeMbas CLI connections.yaml model entry, a LLeMbas model row, and each model LLeMbas serves at /v1/models (where a logged-in CLI configures itself from it). Unknown is not zero: an absent field means nobody has said.

id.description: What is sent as `model` in a request.

family.description: Which prompt overlay the model gets (prompts/family/). Guessed from the id when absent.

context.description: The whole context window in tokens. 0 or absent: unknown — no percentage, no automatic compaction.

max_output.description: The most tokens one reply may have.

temperature.description: The sampling temperature the model is set up with. LLeMbas: the administrator's, which it also applies to a request that does not set one.

efforts.description: The reasoning efforts the model takes, in offering order. Narrowed when a server refuses one (quirks.json effort-refused). Absent: each project's fallback (the CLI's: low, medium, high); [] — the model takes none, and its one effort level is `default`.

thinking_switch.description: Spec 3.2.0: the model's server turns thinking off for a request that sends `chat_template_kwargs.enable_thinking: false` (Qwen3.x and Nemotron 3.x templates on llama.cpp, vLLM, SGLang). Only then is the level `off` offered. Absent: false.

effort.description: The level a new conversation starts with, when it is one of the levels the model offers (see `levels`); otherwise `medium` when the model takes it, else its first effort, else `default`. `off` — thinking switched off — exists only with thinking_switch; `default` — no effort sent, the model's own — only for a model that takes no efforts.

effort_style.description: OpenAI Chat dialect: where the effort goes — top-level `reasoning_effort`, `chat_template_kwargs.reasoning_effort` (all llama.cpp reads), or both (the default).

vision.description: Takes images. Never sent images otherwise: most servers refuse the whole request.

tools.description: Takes tool calls. false: it can only talk; never sent a tools array.

notes.description: What the model is good at, in a line: other models are told about it in the roster, for handing work over.

capacity.description: How much the model's server can do at once, so a helper or a subagent on it is not started where it would evict or wait for the model already working.

group.description: Models that share one server holding one model at a time (llama-swap): starting another model of the group unloads this one. The CLI: a model's `group`, or its connection when the connection sets one_model_at_a_time. LLeMbas: the connection's name when it sets one_model_at_a_time, which is what /v1/models says.

single_session.description: The model serves one request at a time: a second one waits behind the first. The same as `parallel: 1`, which a server that knows `parallel` sends beside it for older clients.

parallel.description: Spec 3.2.0: how many requests the model's server serves at once (llama.cpp's slots, a vLLM or SGLang batch); one more waits behind them. Read as: `parallel` when given, else 1 when single_session is true, else no limit (a hosted API). Where both are given and disagree, `parallel` wins. A team (team.md) is offered only on a model that serves at least 2.

levels.about: Spec 3.2.0. The effort levels a chat offers for a model, in order: `off` when thinking_switch is true, then the model's `efforts` — or, when it takes none, the one level `default`. What each sends (OpenAI chat): `off` — `chat_template_kwargs.enable_thinking: false` and no `reasoning_effort` anywhere; `default` — neither; an effort — `reasoning_effort` where effort_style puts it, and no `enable_thinking`. The Anthropic dialect: `off` sends no `thinking`. A level the model does not offer (an `off` for a model without the switch, from an older client or a stored chat) is read as the start level (`effort`'s rule). How it is shown: one level — no effort control at all; two, one of them `off` — a Thinking on/off switch, on being the other level; more — a slider or a list, in this order. conformance/levels.json.
